In an oncologic patient, every enhancing brain lesion is a metastasis until proven otherwise; lung carcinoma is the most frequent cause. Typical signs: location at the gray-white matter junction or deep, nodular or ring enhancement, vasogenic edema disproportionate to the lesion.
In the report: number (single, few, multiple: decides between surgery, radiosurgery and whole-brain radiotherapy), location and size of each, edema, mass effect (midline shift, ventricles, herniations), hemorrhage. Midline shift is measured at the septum pellucidum relative to the line joining the anterior and posterior attachments of the falx.
Mass effect with subfalcine herniation must be communicated to the treating physician: it changes therapy (steroids) and the timing of surgery.
